evals.name: find-stale-numbers-against-artefacts
evals.prompt: I re-ran the analysis in code/analysis.py and I think the write-up has drifted. Can you check the numbers in paper/main.tex, paper/supplement.tex and paper/cover_letter.md against what results/summary.csv and results/recovery_path.csv actually say? Tell me exactly what's wrong and where.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the scope error (39 to 74 payment range whose 74 comes from a non-building site; correct 39 to 54), the count contradiction (three vs four building sites), the shape claim contradicted by the monotone recovery path, and the unsourced connection-charge figures. Reports file:line.

evals.name: build-a-reusable-gate
evals.prompt: This manuscript keeps going stale every time I re-run the model. I want a check I can run before every submission that fails loudly if a number in the prose stops matching the CSVs. Set it up for this project.
evals.expected_output: Builds a runnable checker over all three documents, wired to recompute values from the CSVs rather than hard-coding them, with patterns that catch new wrong values rather than only known-bad strings, and verifies it fires by breaking a value deliberately.

evals.name: referee-with-artefact-access
evals.prompt: Referee this paper for me the way a hard journal reviewer would. Score it out of 10 and give me major and minor points I can act on.
evals.expected_output: Runs a referee pass that checks claims against the committed CSVs rather than reading the prose alone, scores with a stated band meaning, gives file:line for findings, and flags the untraceable connection-charge figures as the most serious category.
